joints.notes: Vane is a box whose local centre is0.15m below hinge. Apply T(pivot) Rx(q) T(0,-0.15,0). Top-edge location follows rail.

input_rate.note: Peak assumed wind speed corresponds to30degree plate deflection. Wind(t) follows torque relation in motion.

drive.justification: Slow quasi-static wind cycle illustrates an uncalibrated plate. Rate and aerodynamic coefficient are assumed.

joint_values.plate-tilt: q(t)=(pi/12)*(1-cos(2*pi*t/12)), radians. t seconds. Wind magnitude V(t)=sqrt(2*0.12*9.81*sin(q)/(1.225*1.2*0.06*cos(q)^2)), m/s toward-Z. Atq=0,V=0.

motion.visitor_12s: The vane opens smoothly to30degrees and returns once. It reads force, with no invented historical speed scale.

animation_notes: No undocumented flight, lift, bounce, mechanism or invisible reset.
The shown motion is quasi-static. Do not add bounce, direct proportionality between angle and wind speed, or a numbered historical metres-per-second scale.
No propeller or cups. The museum English name Propeller anemometer is inconsistent with its hinged-plate description.

Apply vane transform T([0,-0.04,0])*Rx(q)*T([0,-0.15,0]) relative to rail. Moving eyes inherit the vane transform, fixed pin and eyes inherit rail. Vane X extent +/-0.10 m clears the fixed eyes at +/-0.12 m and quadrant frame at X=0.14 m. Hinge eyes top y=0.771 m remains below rail bottom y=0.78 m except attached hangers.

research.identification: CA 675r, older 249v a/b, verified in the holder-backed joint catalogue and e-Leo [s-holder,s-folio].
sheet_vs_reconstruction: The sheet shows a pressure vane beside other instruments and asks for a clock [s-holder,s-folio].
IBM Italia 1952 created a wooden and copper model. The present metric frame, tick positions and aerodynamic calibration are independent modern choices, not copied dimensions [s-model,a-geometry].

claims.claimed: Measure distance carried per hour by wind, with a clock [s-folio].
claims.built_lifetime: No securely documented lifetime instrument located.
claims.later: IBM 1952 is a display reconstruction, not a reported calibration campaign [s-model].

physics.formula: Approximate plate normal force F=0.5*rho*Cd*A*(V*cos(theta))^2. Torque balance F*l/2 =m*g*l/2*sin(theta). V=sqrt(2*m*g*sin(theta)/(rho*Cd*A*cos(theta)^2)).
physics.inputs: Every numeric input in a-physics. General drag equation s-drag.
physics.results: At theta 30 degrees and the given 0.12 kg, 0.06 m 2 plate, V=4.219 m/s. F=0.5886 N, gravitational restoring torque 0.08829 N m. Angle is not proportional to speed.
physics.limitations: Real plate coefficient varies with inclination and Reynolds number. Hinge friction and gust dynamics omitted. No historical calibration claim.
physics.verdict_en: A 30 degree tilt corresponds to about 4.2 m/s only under this assumed calibration.
physics.verdict_de: 30 Grad Ausschlag entsprechen nur mit dieser angenommenen Kalibrierung etwa 4,2 m/s.

myths.correction: Museo Galileo credits Alberti’s 1450 tablet description before Leonardo [s-history].

research.confidence: High folio and instrument principle. Conditional calibration. All physical construction dimensions assumed.

geometry_validation.method: Local primitive and mesh geometry transformed through the specified joint hierarchy. Forty-nine poses across 12 seconds, or one static pose. Tube centreline bounds conservatively expanded by radius. Analytic motion extrema and attachment clearances are given in animation_notes.
geometry_validation.result: All tested swept points are inside the declared conservative bounding box. Geometry defines a C exhibit interpretation, not structural certification.
